scenes.tts: A fruit fly cell holds eight chromosomes. Its eggs and sperm hold four. Which four? Mendel worked out his laws from counts of peas. He never saw what did the separating. A cell division called meiosis does it.
scenes.visual: Cell with eight chromosomes, a small cell with four question-mark slots, an unknown box between them that turns into meiosis.
scenes.narration: A fruit fly cell holds eight chromosomes. Its eggs and sperm hold four. Which four? Mendel worked out his laws from counts of peas. He never saw what did the separating. A cell division called meiosis does it.

scenes.tts: Follow one pair of homologous chromosomes. Homologs are the two members of a pair, one from each parent. This fly carries two alleles of one gene: capital A on one homolog, small a on the other. In S phase, each chromosome is copied into two sister chromatids. Count centromeres, not arms. It is still one chromosome.
scenes.visual: One pair of homologs, coloured by allele, copies into sister chromatids joined at the centromere.
scenes.caption: Follow one pair of homologous chromosomes. Homologs are the two members of a pair, one from each parent. This fly carries two alleles of one gene: A on one homolog, a on the other. In S phase, each chromosome is copied into two sister chromatids. Count centromeres, not arms. It is still one chromosome.
scenes.narration: Follow one pair of homologous chromosomes. Homologs are the two members of a pair, one from each parent. This fly carries two alleles of one gene: A on one homolog, a on the other. In S phase, each chromosome is copied into two sister chromatids. Count centromeres, not arms. It is still one chromosome.

scenes.tts: Meiosis is one round of DNA replication followed by two divisions. In prophase one, homologs pair along their length, as a bivalent. At metaphase one, the two homologs face opposite poles. Anaphase one pulls them apart, so capital A and small a go to different cells.
scenes.visual: Homologs pair, line up facing opposite poles, and are pulled to two cells.
scenes.caption: Meiosis is one round of DNA replication followed by two divisions. In prophase I, homologs pair along their length, as a bivalent. At metaphase I, the two homologs face opposite poles. Anaphase I pulls them apart, so A and a go to different cells.
scenes.narration: Meiosis is one round of DNA replication followed by two divisions. In prophase I, homologs pair along their length, as a bivalent. At metaphase I, the two homologs face opposite poles. Anaphase I pulls them apart, so A and a go to different cells.

scenes.tts: Count the centromeres again. Each cell has one chromosome of this pair, so each is already haploid. The chromosome still has two sister chromatids, and no copying comes before meiosis two. Meiosis two pulls the sisters apart, as a mitosis would. Two of the four products carry capital A, and two carry small a. That is the law of segregation, seen as chromosome movement.
scenes.visual: Sisters part in the two cells, giving four products, two with A and two with a.
scenes.caption: Count the centromeres again. Each cell has one chromosome of this pair, so each is already haploid. The chromosome still has two sister chromatids, and no copying comes before meiosis II. Meiosis II pulls the sisters apart, as a mitosis would. Two of the four products carry A, and two carry a. That is the law of segregation, seen as chromosome movement.

scenes.tts: Now add a second gene, with alleles capital B and small b, on a different chromosome. Each pair can face the spindle two ways, and how one pair faces does not affect how another does. In one meiosis, the four products are two capital A capital B, and two small a small b. In another, they are two capital A small b, and two small a capital B. Ignore crossing over.
scenes.visual: Two bivalents on the metaphase plate flip independently; each orientation gives two kinds of product.
scenes.caption: Now add a second gene, with alleles B and b, on a different chromosome. Each pair can face the spindle two ways, and how one pair faces does not affect how another does. In one meiosis, the four products are two AB, and two ab. In another, they are two Ab, and two aB. Ignore crossing over.
scenes.narration: Now add a second gene, with alleles B and b, on a different chromosome. Each pair can face the spindle two ways, and how one pair faces does not affect how another does. In one meiosis, the four products are two AB, and two ab. In another, they are two Ab, and two aB. Ignore crossing over.

scenes.tts: Across many meioses, the two orientations are equally likely, so each of the four kinds makes up one quarter. With four pairs, the fly has two times two times two times two, or sixteen chromosome combinations, ignoring crossing over. Pairs orient on their own at metaphase one. Remember the rule: meiosis one separates homologs, and meiosis two separates sisters.
scenes.visual: Four equal bars, sixteen combinations built by doubling, then three panels: orient, homologs part, sisters part.
scenes.caption: Across many meioses, the two orientations are equally likely, so each of the four kinds makes up one quarter. Remember the rule: meiosis I separates homologs, and meiosis II separates sisters.
